messages:
Taylor: Heads-up bringing halberd18b-int4 into dedicated canary, seeing intermittent OOMs under steady chat load (avg input ~350 tokens).
Ash: how frequent and which pool?
Taylor: canary pool only, ~2 OOMs in first 12m.
Taylor: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-22T15:12:04Z] ERROR oom: alloc failed at kv_cache_grow
model=halberd18b-int4 pool=gpu0
config: batch_size=4, window=12, max_new_tokens=1024, prefetch=true, slot_reserve=0.05
trace: alloc 3.2GB -> failed
```
infra-bot: canary-run-id=cr-20260322-halb-01 status=failed runtime-version=0.14.0 events=2
Mira: int4 + max_new_tokens=1024 = fragmentation risk for 18b-family.
Kevin: on similar models we cap batch_size=2 and default max_new_tokens=512 during warmup; slot_reserve bump to 0.12 helped.
Taylor: micro-bench vs int8 (50 prompts): int8 p50=210ms tokens/s=280, int4 p50=230ms tokens/s=300. Quick eval (100 prompts) shows ~-1.8% rouge-L for int4.
Ash: small perf gain but quality dip + frag risk. Not a slam dunk.
Mira: mitigation options: lower max_new_tokens default, increase slot_reserve, enable soft-evict/kv-trim, or mixed-fallback to int8 for critical routes.
Kevin: note runtime 0.14.0 misses slab compaction and soft-evict flags in 0.14.2. Canary is on older runtime.
infra-bot: runtime-version=0.14.0 for cr-20260322-halb-01
Ash: plan: upgrade canary to 0.14.2, soak 2h with config: max_new_tokens=512, batch_size=2, slot_reserve=0.12, session_cache=false, kv_trim_threshold=0.6, adaptive_window=enabled. Add OOM+latency alerts.
Taylor: repro curl used for testing included max_new_tokens=1024; I'll run new repros with 512 and session_cache=false.
Kevin: also try disabling prefetch to isolate prefetch-induced KV churn. If still OOMs, I'll bisect quant packer per-layer.
Mira: after soak run paired 500-prompt eval: int8 baseline vs int4 candidate. If int4 regression >1% rouge-L, plan mixed fallback or revert.
infra-bot: soak job queued: soak-1849999999-1 owner=Taylor team=eng-ml
Ash: add alerts: OOM spike >1/min, p95 latency >1s, alert to #release-war-room and eng-oncall.
Kevin: FYI we saw long-tail activations on halberd family in quant calib. soft-evict + slab compaction should help.
Taylor: starting soak in ~10m. Will post results here.
Mira: assign followups: Taylor=soak+eval, Kevin=runtime upgrade + packer bisect if needed, Ash=alerts+dashboards.
Taylor: Thanks — kicking off. Will update with results and eval numbers.
